title: Oven Smoked Brisket
description: It might sound basic, but this cooking method yields a meat that everyone loves.
time_estimate: About 8–9 hours (bakes low and slow at 225°F)
steps: Rub both sides of the Brisket with oil. Combine sugar, paprika, salt and black pepper in a small bowl and rub on meat. Place brisket in a baking pan, fat side up.

Cover very well (2 layers of foil) and bake for 8-9 hours on 225⁰F. (In the original recipe in Dinner Done, we wrote to remove the brisket from the pan and bake it on 425⁰F, uncovered, for 8 minutes. While it gives it a nice crust, we found it wasn’t a must and on Yom Tov is impractical, so we skipped this step this time).
At this point, you can remove the brisket from the pan and wrap it in baking paper and then foil. You can refrigerate or freeze it if not eating right away.

To rewarm, add 1-inch apple juice (or light grape juice) into the bottom of a pan. Wrap brisket loosely in foil and place in pan. Place in oven for 10 minutes, or until warm. If your oven is on a very low temp, you can cover and bake longer until warm.

clipping_notes.label: Note
clipping_notes.text: You can omit the paprika and black pepper and replace with a tablespoon of instant coffee.

clipping_notes.label: Make ahead
clipping_notes.text: Because I make this brisket so often, rather than start from scratch every time, I prepare 4 at a time. After cooking, let cool and freeze. Then, vacuum seal (or ziplock) the brisket, or wrap it in baking paper and then foil like a package. On Shabbos morning, I place the brisket on top of the Crock Pot to warm. I slice and serve it as a main dish alongside the cholent.
